cfb-2017-09-02-wnmu-usd: San Diego opened its 2017 season with a 34–20 victory over Western New Mexico at Torero Stadium, overcoming a 13–0 first-quarter deficit. The Mustangs struck first behind [[cfb-wnmu-javia-hall|Javia Hall]], but [[cfb-usd-anthony-lawrence|Anthony Lawrence]] immediately connected with [[cfb-usd-justin-priest|Justin Priest]] for a 58-yard touchdown. The Toreros added a field goal before the quarter ended, then took a 17–13 halftime lead and eventually scored 27 unanswered points.

Lawrence finished 15-for-28 for 187 yards and two touchdowns, including a two-yard scoring pass to Ross Dwelley in the third quarter. Freshman [[cfb-usd-emilio-martinez|Emilio Martinez]] ran 17 times for 96 yards and sealed the win with a 13-yard touchdown after Western New Mexico cut the lead to 27–20 in the fourth. Priest caught four passes for 95 yards and a score, while [[cfb-usd-kim-mahoney|Kim Mahoney]] contributed eight tackles as San Diego recovered five Mustang fumbles.

Western New Mexico actually outgained San Diego 506–339. Hall threw for 464 yards and three touchdowns, while [[cfb-wnmu-d-angelo-bowie|D'Angelo Bowie]] caught 19 passes for 263 yards and two scores, including an 86-yard fourth-quarter touchdown. The Toreros' five takeaways proved decisive in a game where the visitors produced more yardage but could not protect the football.
cfb-2017-09-23-butler-usd: San Diego opened Pioneer Football League play with a 38–17 victory over Butler at Torero Stadium, powered by a five-touchdown afternoon from [[cfb-usd-anthony-lawrence|Anthony Lawrence]]. The quarterback completed 26 of 39 passes for 367 yards without an interception, and the Toreros amassed 499 yards of offense. The win extended San Diego's conference home winning streak to 28 games.

[[cfb-usd-justin-priest|Justin Priest]] caught nine passes for 148 yards and three touchdowns, including the game's opening score. Butler answered with two touchdown connections between [[cfb-butler-will-marty|Will Marty]] and [[cfb-butler-pace-temple|Pace Temple]], pulling within 17–14 early in the second quarter. Lawrence responded with two more touchdown passes before halftime, including a 13-yard strike to [[cfb-usd-ross-dwelley|Ross Dwelley]] with 44 seconds remaining, and San Diego carried a 31–14 lead into the break.

Butler managed only a field goal after halftime. Marty finished with 260 passing yards, and Temple caught eight passes for 155 yards and both Bulldog touchdowns. Dwelley supplied six catches for 101 yards for San Diego, while [[cfb-usd-emilio-martinez|Emilio Martinez]] ran for 93 yards, including a 52-yard fourth-quarter gain that set up the Toreros' final field goal.
